title: Signed operating policy v2 (no fields exist for UA/fingerprint/webdriver/proxy/captcha automation)
description: v1.3 (B-23, B-07, B-22, C-26, C-31, C-06, C-17; re-audit E-04, E-05, E-17). Schema bounds are the outer fence; the engine additionally clamps every field to the app-embedded PORTAL_MODE_CEILING / CAPTCHA_RELAY_CEILING / POLICY_FLOOR (design/03-engine.md §7.1) and journals policy.clamped; if a [min, max] pair (stepDelayMs, afterNavSettleMs, daemon.gapBetweenRunsMin) ends up with max < min after clamping, max := min (lower bound wins). SIGNATURES: `signatures` (2-of-3 distinct pinned policy keys, or the single pinned emergency key) cover the CONTENT digest = JCS(policy without `signatures`, `issuedAt`, `expiresAt`, `timestamp`); any content change bumps `monotonic`. FRESHNESS: `issuedAt`/`expiresAt` are covered by `timestamp`, signed by the online timestamp key (HSM, automatic) over JCS({contentDigest, monotonic, issuedAt, expiresAt}); a content-unchanged re-issue is a new `timestamp` every 48 h (no human quorum). Engine-only checks: expiresAt - issuedAt <= 72h (POLICY_MAX_VALIDITY_H; the package index keeps 14 days); issuedAt > now + 5 min => reject (policy.issued_in_future); version comparison only within the same keyEpoch and new monotonic <= stored + 1000 (registry.version_jump_rejected). EMERGENCY KEY: a policy carrying only the emergency-key content signature is accepted only if EVERY field moves in the conservative direction and at least one strictly (portalMode down only; captchaRelay toward disabled only; limits.* <=; cooldown.onBlockSignalHours >=; positiveDetectionsForCooldown <=; onCaptchaBurst.count <=, windowMin >=; blockSignalsAdd superset; pace.* >=; run.* <=; retries.stepMax <=, baseMs/capMs >=; remote.irreversiblePerDay <=; remote.minProtocolVersion >=; remote.disabledFeatures and notifyOnIrreversible superset; queue.* <=; verify.minElapsedMs >=, lookups >=; daemon intervals >=; every other field equal), else policy.rejected_not_conservative. Missing portal key in any portal map => that portal is postprocess (fail-closed). A rejected policy file => keep the last valid policy. EXPIRY: an expired policy is NOT replaced by all-postprocess immediately; the engine keeps the last valid policy, refuses relaxation, stops the daemon and refuses hotfix loads (policy.stale); 168 h after expiry => all portals postprocess. With no valid policy ever installed => most conservative built-in policy (all portals postprocess).

expiresAt.description: <= 72 hours after issuedAt (engine check). Expired => keep last valid policy, no relaxation, daemon stopped, hotfix loads refused; 168 h after expiry => all portals postprocess

timestamp.description: Freshness signature by the online timestamp key over JCS({contentDigest, monotonic, issuedAt, expiresAt}). Required for issuedAt/expiresAt to be trusted; re-issued every 48 h without changing content (E-05).

commitWindowMs.description: Upper bound only. Token exp = approval + min(commitWindowMs, static bound of W(X)) (R-G8). Validator checks commitWindowMs >= signFlow.maxWaitMs + verify upper bound.

blockSignalsAdd.description: Deterministic block-signal dictionary ADDITIONS (C-24). Union with the app-embedded dictionary; a policy cannot remove built-in entries.

verify.description: B-07 absence-of-evidence requirements for verify not_committed.

remote.description: C-06, C-31. Remote (phone) approval limits and protocol kill switch.

signatures.description: Content signatures (see top-level description): 2-of-3 distinct pinned policy keys; exactly 1 signature is allowed only from the pinned emergency key and only for strictly more conservative policies (field-by-field rule in design/03-engine.md §7.1).

keyEventDelayMs.description: Enforced by the vault typist itself inside a secret window (A-26); the engine never sees per-key timing.
